title: Agoh 2026 Alternating-Sum Conjecture: Counterexample Map
description: A source-bound map separating the published conjecture, explicit n=2 counterexample, exact algebraic certificate, stronger finite-difference theorem, and unresolved priority review.

metadata.priority_caveat: No correction or resolution was found in targeted searches; author/editor confirmation remains external work.

nodes.label: Agoh 2026 paper
nodes.statement: INTEGERS 26 (2026), A9 defines Q_n and states the final factor-characterization conjecture.

nodes.label: Agoh factor-characterization conjecture
nodes.statement: For nonzero real-rooted f, the numerator of Q_n has at least (x-1)^n iff f is a monomial or has only simple roots different from 1.

nodes.label: Repeated-root test polynomial
nodes.statement: Take f(t)=(t-2)^2 and n=2; f is real-rooted with a repeated root and is not a monomial.

nodes.label: Load-bearing numerator factorization
nodes.statement: N=(x-1)^2(x^4-2x^3-7x^2+4x+12), with denominator value 1 and cofactor value 8 at x=1.
nodes.formalization_status: Lean algebraic identity plus exact arithmetic certificate

nodes.label: General finite-difference divisibility theorem
nodes.statement: For every polynomial f with f(1) nonzero and every n>=0, the reduced numerator of Q_n is divisible by (x-1)^n.
nodes.notes: Proof uses h(t)=1/f(exp t) and the nth finite difference identity. Full all-n theorem is not yet formalized in Lean.
nodes.formalization_status: human deductive proof; finite identity regression-tested

nodes.label: The repeated-root example works exactly for every n
nodes.statement: For f(t)=(t-2)^2, the reduced numerator of Q_n has a zero of exactly order n at x=1 for every n>=1.
nodes.notes: The nth derivative at zero of 1/(2-exp(t))^2 is a strictly positive convergent series, so the first surviving finite-difference coefficient is nonzero.
nodes.formalization_status: human deductive proof; not yet formalized in Lean

nodes.label: Natural-domain correction
nodes.statement: The definition requires f(1) nonzero because its i=0 summand is 1/f(1); the printed nonzero real-rooted domain does not ensure this.

nodes.label: Exact-order replacement criterion
nodes.statement: For f(1) nonzero, the zero of Q_n at x=1 has exact order n iff ((t d/dt)^n (1/f(t))) evaluated at t=1 is nonzero.
nodes.notes: This reframes the meaningful successor problem as classifying excess multiplicity.
nodes.formalization_status: human deductive proof; not yet formalized in Lean

nodes.label: Only-if direction is false
nodes.statement: The repeated-root polynomial f(t)=(t-2)^2 satisfies the asserted numerator divisibility, so the conjectured only-if classification is false.

nodes.label: External novelty and priority review
nodes.statement: Confirm with the author/editor and a broader expert literature review that the disproof has not already been reported.
nodes.notes: This does not affect the internal mathematical validity of the counterexample.

edges.notes: Constrains novelty/priority only, not the algebraic disproof.
